text.p: Caterpillar Inc said Friay it signed individual master sponsored research agreements with the University of Illinois, Carnegie Mellon University and Purdue University.

"Working with these universities as extensions of our own research facilities will result in even further technological innovations to our products, ultimately benefiting our customers," Gerald Palmer, vice president of technical services said.

Caterpillar, which makes construction and mining equiment and diesel engines, said the agreements will give it access to the universities for better facilitation of research projects, continuing education, recruiting and exchange of personnel for specific projects.

"By understanding Caterpillar's future objectives, we hope to create new technologies and processes that will have a positive impact on Caterpillar's meeting those objectives while advancing the education, research and technology transfer missions of the university," Paul Christiano, provost of Carnegie Mellon in Pittsburgh, said in a statement.
